requirements.requirement: The system must return a provider reputation_score field in the Evaluate Care API response when aggregated ratings data exists.
The system must include source_count metadata indicating the number of rating sources contributing to the reputation score.
The system must include last_updated timestamp metadata reflecting the most recent aggregation computation time.
The system must retrieve aggregated ratings data via the service implemented in EVAL-P5-S2 using provider NPI as the lookup key.
The system must preserve existing Evaluate Care API response structure and not remove or rename pre-existing fields.
The system must expose reputation_score as a normalized numeric value between 0 and 1 inclusive.
The system must omit or null the reputation_score field when no ratings data is available for the provider.
The system must return source_count as 0 when no ratings sources are available.
The system must ensure the API response remains valid JSON and conforms to existing response schema contracts used by tool routing.
The system must complete aggregation data retrieval and response construction within existing Evaluate Care API latency thresholds.
The system must handle service unavailability from the aggregation logic by returning the response without reputation fields and without failing the entire request.
The system must log an error event when aggregation data retrieval fails.
The system must ensure compatibility with existing tool routing by not altering routing keys or tool identifiers in the response.
The system must ensure that any LLM consuming the API can reliably parse reputation_score, source_count, and last_updated as distinct structured fields.
The system must provide consistent field naming conventions aligned with existing Evaluate Care response schemas to support LLM grounding.
The system must ensure reputation_score is deterministic for the same input data across repeated API calls.
The system must ensure that missing metadata fields do not cause downstream LLM tool failures or parsing errors.
The system must include aggregation metadata only when the Evaluate Care API is invoked for provider entities and not for unrelated entity types.
